Meanwhile, *The Lost Boys* brings vampire mythology to the musical stage with visual spectacle and a rock score that finally gives Broadway its long-awaited undead musical moment.

Not every production is finding success, however. *Beaches, A New Musical* represents the season's most notable disappointment, with critics finding the adaptation overwhelmed by schmaltz despite Jessica Vosk's acclaimed performance. The Studio 54 revival of *The Rocky Horror Show* earns praise for its energy and cast but raises questions about whether the cult classic's transgressive edge can still shock in 2026.

Whether you're drawn to daring reinventions or nostalgic revivals, the top-rated musicals this season offer a snapshot of Broadway at its most adventurous—and most uneven.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
As we look back at the Broadway shows that opened in 2020—a year that would soon see theaters go dark for an unprecedented period—the productions that premiered before the shutdown offer a fascinating snapshot of the season's ambitions. Six years later, these shows remain significant markers in Broadway history, representing the last wave of productions before the pandemic reshaped the industry.

Charles Fuller's "A Soldier's Play" stands as the highest-rated production from this period, bringing the Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway for the first time decades after its original off-Broadway run. Critics consistently praise the production's powerful performances and the play's enduring examination of race and justice within the military. The revival demonstrates how classic American drama continues to resonate with contemporary audiences.

Ivo van Hove's reimagining of "West Side Story" proves more divisive, earning mixed reactions for its bold departure from Jerome Robbins' iconic choreography and its incorporation of video elements. While some critics applaud the fresh approach to the beloved musical, others question whether the experimental staging serves the material. Bess Wohl's "Grand Horizons" offers a different flavor entirely—a Neil Simon-esque comedy exploring late-life divorce that benefits from strong ensemble work.

The average critic score of 74 across these productions reflects a season of solid, if not universally acclaimed, work. Laura Linney's performance in "My Name is Lucy Barton" earns particular mention as a highlight, even among critics who find the Elizabeth Strout adaptation itself uneven.

For theatergoers interested in exploring these pre-pandemic productions, our detailed reviews and ratings below provide comprehensive guidance on what to expect from each show.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
As we reach May 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2021 continue to demonstrate the remarkable resilience and artistic innovation that defined the theater industry's return following the pandemic shutdown. That season marked a watershed moment for American theater, producing some of the most daring and critically acclaimed work in recent Broadway history.

Leading the critical rankings is "Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club," Rebecca Frecknall's immersive revival that transforms the August Wilson Theatre into the decadent nightclub itself. Critics consistently praise this production as a theatrical triumph that reimagines the classic musical for contemporary audiences. Close behind is "The Lehman Trilogy," Sam Mendes' epic examination of American capitalism that compresses 164 years of history into a single evening, powered by three virtuosic performances. Meanwhile, "Dana H." stands out as perhaps the season's most unconventional offering—a mesmerizing thriller featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance that challenges traditional notions of theatrical storytelling.

The 2021 season also showcased vital new voices and bold revivals, from Jeremy O. Harris's provocative "Slave Play" to Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped "Company," which arrived as a poignant tribute following Stephen Sondheim's passing. The top-rated shows from this season maintain an impressive average critic score of 82 out of 100, reflecting the consistently high quality of work that emerged during this pivotal period.

Whether you're drawn to immersive experiences, intimate character studies, or bold social commentary, the highest-rated plays from 2021 offer a snapshot of Broadway at its most adventurous and essential. Explore the rankings below to find your next theatrical experience.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
Four years after their premieres, the best Broadway plays from 2022's remarkable season continue to resonate with audiences in May 2026. That year marked a creative renaissance for theater, delivering an exceptional crop of productions that pushed boundaries, revived classics, and reminded audiences why live performance remains irreplaceable.

Leading the critical pack, **Kimberly Akimbo** stands as a testament to Broadway's ability to find profound beauty in unexpected places. This musical about a teenage girl with a rare aging condition balances sharp comedy with devastating emotional truth, earning near-universal acclaim for its originality and heart. Equally groundbreaking, **A Strange Loop** brought Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning vision to Broadway with unflinching honesty, offering a radical meta-musical that challenges audiences while delivering an entirely fresh theatrical experience.

The year also saw Broadway honor its legends. **Into the Woods** emerged as a stripped-down revival that proved Sondheim's genius needs no embellishment, while Tom Stoppard's **Leopoldstadt** offered the playwright's most personal work—a sweeping family saga that confronts the Holocaust with emotional power and intellectual rigor. Meanwhile, revivals of Pulitzer winners **Topdog/Underdog** and **How I Learned to Drive** demonstrated how essential American plays maintain their urgency across decades.

The 2022 class achieves an impressive 84/100 average critic score, reflecting a season where artistic ambition met execution at the highest level. From Mike Birbiglia's intimate storytelling to Jordan E. Cooper's audacious satire **Ain't No Mo'**, these productions represent Broadway firing on all cylinders—taking risks, celebrating masters, and creating space for new voices. Explore the top-rated shows from this exceptional vintage to discover which productions continue to define contemporary theater.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
As May 2026 arrives, the Broadway shows that opened in 2023 continue to demonstrate the remarkable diversity and vitality of that theatrical season. From intimate solo performances to spectacular West End transfers, these productions represent a cross-section of contemporary theater at its finest, with an impressive average critic score of 84 out of 100.

Leading the pack is "Operation Mincemeat," the scrappy British musical that proves you don't need a massive budget to create theatrical magic. Critics consistently praise its five-person ensemble for transforming a peculiar World War II espionage tale into an anarchic, joyously inventive evening that honors both its West End roots and Broadway's grand traditions. Close behind, "Buena Vista Social Club" brings infectious Cuban rhythms to the stage, while Maria Friedman's revival of "Merrily We Roll Along" has finally given Sondheim's once-maligned musical the production it always deserved, earning widespread acclaim for its emotional depth and stellar performances.

The season's strength extends beyond musicals. "Appropriate" emerges as a searing family drama that critics are calling a modern masterpiece, while "Purlie Victorious" proves that Ossie Davis's 1961 satire remains bracingly relevant more than six decades later. Jodie Comer's Broadway debut in "Prima Facie" showcases the power of solo performance, as does Alex Edelman's "Just for Us," which balances humor with provocative cultural commentary.

Whether you're drawn to the theatrical spectacle of "Stranger Things: The First Shadow," the timely resonance of "Parade," or the audacious reimagining of "Fat Ham," the top-rated shows from 2023's Broadway season offer something for every theatergoer's taste and sensibility.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
The 2024 Broadway season continues to resonate strongly with critics nearly two years after these productions first opened their doors. With an impressive average score of 84/100, the class of 2024 demonstrates remarkable staying power, offering theatergoers a diverse array of experiences from intimate character studies to bold reimaginings of classic material.

Leading the critical pack is Matthew Bourne's revival of *Oliver!*, which earns the highest marks for its inventive staging and standout performances. Close behind, *Stereophonic* maintains its position as one of the season's most acclaimed productions, with David Adjmi's three-hour backstage drama about a 1970s rock band continuing to captivate audiences with its immersive authenticity and meticulous attention to the creative process. Cole Escola's *Oh, Mary!* rounds out the top tier, proving that audacious comedy has a firm place among Broadway's critical darlings—the irreverent take on Mary Todd Lincoln delights with its fearless absurdity.

The season's strength lies in its remarkable range. Audiences can experience everything from the ballroom-infused energy of *CATS: The Jellicle Ball* to the tender robot romance of *Maybe Happy Ending*, from Audra McDonald's powerhouse performance in *Gypsy* to the earnest historical storytelling of *Suffs*. Intimate dramas like *Mary Jane* share the spotlight with spectacular crowd-pleasers like *Death Becomes Her*, demonstrating that quality theater comes in many forms.

Whether you're drawn to innovative revivals, original stories, or bold reinterpretations of familiar material, the top-rated shows from 2024 offer compelling reasons to experience Broadway at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
Broadway's 2025 season continues to resonate with audiences this May 2026, delivering an impressive array of productions that have earned widespread critical acclaim. With an average critic score of 86 out of 100, the year's offerings demonstrate remarkable artistic ambition across revivals and new works alike.

Leading the pack is a charming 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee**, which captures critics' hearts with its tender humor and phenomenal performances. Close behind, **Paddington The Musical** delights reviewers with its triumphantly realized puppet protagonist, proving that family-friendly fare can achieve both technical brilliance and emotional depth. Ivo van Hove's searing take on Arthur Miller's **All My Sons** rounds out the top tier, with critics praising Bryan Cranston's performance and the production's devastating emotional power.

The season showcases notable diversity in programming, from beloved family properties like **My Neighbour Totoro** to bold original works such as **Dead Outlaw**, a darkly comic musical about bumbling outlaw Elmer McCurdy that critics describe as deliciously macabre. Classic musicals also make strong showings, with revivals of **The Producers**, **Ragtime**, and **Into the Woods** earning praise for their fresh interpretations and stellar performances. Meanwhile, **Liberation**, David Wohl's memory play about 1970s feminism, demonstrates Broadway's continued engagement with timely social themes.

The strength of these productions reflects a Broadway season firing on all cylinders, balancing nostalgia with innovation and spectacle with substance. Whether you're drawn to intimate character studies or grand musical spectacles, explore the top-rated shows from 2025 to discover what's captured critics' attention and continues to pack houses this spring.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
Broadway's 2026 season is proving to be a year of striking revivals and compelling new voices, with classic American drama leading the critical conversation this May. The season's standout productions demonstrate the enduring power of theatrical storytelling, from mid-century masterworks to intimate contemporary pieces.

Nathan Lane commands the stage in Joe Mantello's stark revival of *Death of a Salesman*, earning the highest critical praise of the year. Critics find fresh urgency in Arthur Miller's classic, with Lane's electrifying performance anchoring a production that feels both timeless and remarkably current. The revival demonstrates how great plays continue to reveal new depths with each generation.

New work is also making its mark, particularly Gina Gionfriddo's *Becky Shaw*, a razor-sharp dark comedy that has won acclaim for its incisive examination of family dynamics and modern relationships. Meanwhile, Daniel Radcliffe brings warmth and vulnerability to the interactive solo show *Every Brilliant Thing*, creating an intimate theatrical experience that critics describe as life-affirming despite its difficult subject matter.

The season's strong average critic score reflects a healthy mix of established playwrights and fresh perspectives, from David Lindsay-Abaire's biting HOA satire *The Balusters* to August Wilson's *Joe Turner's Come and Gone* receiving renewed attention under Debbie Allen's direction. Even lesser-known works like Noël Coward's *Fallen Angels* are finding new audiences through spirited performances.

Whether you're drawn to canonical American drama, sharp contemporary writing, or rediscovered classics, the top-rated productions opening this year offer theatergoers substantial material and memorable performances worth experiencing live.

broadway-shows-closing-soon.intro:
As May 2026 unfolds, several noteworthy Broadway productions are preparing to take their final bows, offering theater enthusiasts a last chance to catch some of the season's most talked-about work.

Leading the pack of closing shows is **Becky Shaw**, Gina Gionfriddo's razor-sharp dark comedy that has earned the strongest critical reception among departing productions. The play's incisive exploration of a disastrous blind date and its ripple effects through fractured family relationships has resonated with critics who praise its wit and emotional complexity.

Daniel Radcliffe brings warmth and accessibility to **Every Brilliant Thing**, the interactive solo show about depression, resilience, and finding joy in life's small moments. The production's intimate format and life-affirming message have made it a standout among this season's more personal theatrical experiences.

Comedy takes center stage with both **The Balusters**, David Lindsay-Abaire's biting satire of homeowners association politics featuring a strong ensemble cast, and **Fallen Angels**, a rare Noël Coward revival that showcases Catherine O'Hara and Rose Byrne's acclaimed comedic chemistry and masterful drunk-acting in this fizzy 1920s romp.

Drama lovers still have time to witness John Lithgow's towering performance as Roald Dahl in **Giant**, which critics describe as fearless and commanding, while Adrien Brody makes his Broadway debut in **The Fear of 13**, a wrongful conviction drama that has drawn praise for his intense performance despite mixed reviews overall.

The closing shows span a wide range of theatrical styles and tones, from intimate one-person shows to ensemble comedies and biographical dramas. Check individual show pages for exact closing dates and remaining ticket availability.
